titolo: Trump, Putin and Xi in One Room: The Summit Allies Fear
angolo: The handshake before the talks: why Trump's first-ever three-way summit with Putin and Xi has allies on edge, and what is actually on the table in Shenzhen.
descrizione: Trump, Putin and Xi in One Room: The Summit Allies Fear. Donald Trump landed in Shenzhen, shook hands with Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping, and now faces the first-ever three-way summit of the world's biggest military powers. On the table: nuclear arms after New START expired, the Iran war, and, by Trump's own words, Ukraine. Allies in Europe and Asia are uneasy, and Kyiv says nothing about Ukraine should be decided without Ukraine. Subscribe, because this story is still moving.

scene.testo: Wednesday. Shenzhen, China. Donald Trump arrives for the APEC summit.
Xi Jinping is waiting at the bottom of the stairs.
Hours later, Trump shakes hands with Vladimir Putin at the APEC welcome banquet.
Three leaders. Three nuclear giants. One stage.
Al Jazeera calls it the first ever three-way meeting between the leaders of the world's three most powerful militaries.
And, according to Axios, America's own allies are watching with unease.
Why are they uneasy? We'll get to that. First, what just happened.
Can Donald Trump sit between Putin and Xi without his allies worrying about the outcome?
Stay with me. In a minute, you'll see a gesture Xi did not extend to Putin.
THE HUG ON THE TARMAC
Trump landed at Shenzhen's Bao'an airport on Wednesday morning, ahead of the talks.
Xi greeted him on the tarmac. A hug, a few words.
Newsweek reports it was the first time Xi had greeted a foreign head of state that way as president.
It reciprocated Trump's own gesture at Joint Base Andrews in September, according to Axios and NPR.
Putin got no personal greeting from Xi. He was met instead by Cai Qi, a senior Communist Party official.
Then came the handshake the whole world was waiting for.
Before the APEC welcome banquet, Trump and Putin shook hands as Xi looked on.
The real talks begin Thursday. And the clock is short.
The Kremlin says one hour is set aside for the three-way meeting, according to Russian officials quoted by Moscow Times.
One hour. For nuclear arms, Iran, and possibly Ukraine.
THE SPEECHES BEFORE THE STORM
But before Trump landed, Xi and Putin had already spoken.
Xi pledged to stand up against trade protectionism, according to Reuters.
Putin followed him on stage and described Western powers as "former hegemons."
He said Europe was in a "humiliating decline" and that sanctions on Russia had backfired. Russia says they made it stronger.
And there was a twist. According to Reuters, Putin spoke after Ukraine's strike on the Kerch bridge.
Reuters reports Ukraine crippled the Kerch road bridge linking Crimea to Russia.
A major blow to a four-year war, Reuters writes.
Xi and Putin then held talks on the sidelines of the summit. They called for a "multipolar world."
Xi called for China and Russia to "lead and advance the trend towards a multipolar world," according to Al Jazeera.
So what is actually on Thursday's table? Three things.
THREE ITEMS ON THE TABLE
Number one: nuclear weapons. The last treaty between the US and Russia expired in February.
It was called New START. First signed in 2010, it capped US and Russian arsenals.
Its lapse left the biggest arsenals without legally binding limits, according to reports.

grafica.sopra: FIRST TIME WITHOUT LIMITS IN HALF A CENTURY

scene.testo: Al Jazeera says the White House has said Trump plans to discuss a possible three-way agreement on nuclear armament.
Number two: the Iran war. Observers call the US-Iran deadlock a "frozen war."
Al Jazeera says talks are stuck on whether to start with Hormuz and incentives, or Iran's nuclear programme.
Washington would like Beijing to privately urge Tehran to compromise, per an analyst quoted by Al Jazeera.
Number three: Ukraine. And here, the story gets complicated.
White House officials said Ukraine would not be on the agenda.
Axios reports a US official said Trump will hold a one-on-one meeting with Putin on Thursday, on the sidelines of the summit.
A US official told Axios that Trump will hold a one-on-one meeting with Putin on Thursday.
Now, the question you've been waiting for: why are allies afraid?
THE ROOM WITHOUT UKRAINE
Axios reports that allies fear Trump could depart from the summit's nuclear agenda and take positions on Ukraine or Taiwan that undermine their interests.
Some people Axios spoke to invoked "Yalta II," recalling the 1945 summit that shaped post-war Europe.
Zelensky used a similar warning on October 28, telling journalists he did not want a "Yalta 2, 3, 4."
Kyiv's message is simple: no decisions about Ukraine without Ukraine.
German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said the message to Trump before he meets Putin is: "No surprises, please."
Axios quotes a European diplomat: every time Trump talks to or sees Putin, it translates into bad news for Ukraine and Europe.
Trump had met key regional allies in Manila before flying to China, according to Reuters.
According to Axios, US officials tried to play down the summit and lower expectations for substantive results.
Trump says meeting both leaders at once makes sense because their countries work together.
WHAT COMES NEXT
On the same day, Trump's envoys Kushner and Witkoff are expected in Berlin, according to Axios.
Zelensky said US representatives will attend meetings in Berlin on Thursday and brief Ukraine on Trump's talks in China.
The White House says Putin agreed to let Europeans join the talks, but Kremlin adviser Ushakov said no such agreement had been reached.
Experts have kept expectations low for major breakthroughs, according to AP.
AP says it could mark a pivot in world history, or become a quickly forgotten photo op.
Zelensky told NBC that Trump and Xi have "enough power to stop Putin" in one meeting.
So the question for Thursday: will allies hear a deal, or a surprise?
The story is still moving. Subscribe, so you don't miss what comes out of Shenzhen.
